prompt: Draw the entire two-direction animation sheet for existing game creature MON-109-0 from these two identity references. Image 1 is its canonical FRONT at rest, image 2 is its old approximate rear and may be misleading. Preserve the exact anatomy and colors in image 1. FOUR large OUTER angular pale walking supports with dark curved tips around the narrow brown/ridged central body. ALSO preserve its original short central pale front/downward appendage as drawn in front identity reference; do not erase it, duplicate it or turn it into an extra long walking leg. Preserve the brown dorsal ridges, original small front shape, pale bent limb segments and dark ends. Compact four-outer-support walking, original leg lengths and body proportions, little bob. No ivory flat body copied from the other reference, extra head, eyes, horns, shell, wings, tail, equipment or human hands. Correct directional anatomy where necessary. Use fixed slightly elevated square-grid camera. EXACTLY FOUR columns and FOUR rows of equal cells, sixteen complete figures. FIRST TWO ROWS: eight poses all walking TOWARD the camera, down the screen. LAST TWO ROWS: eight poses all traveling AWAY, up the screen, viewed from behind. The rear must show true back or tail, not face, chest, or a flipped front. Preserve equipment on the same anatomical side and respect occlusion. Each two-row block is a short continuous cycle: first row support A, load A, swing B, settle B; second row support B, load B, swing A, settle A. For no-leg creatures interpret these as alternating travel phases of their original body. Keep the same scale, silhouette and head position, small grounded motion where appropriate. All 16 separate figures are drawn whole, centered and fully inside their respective cells, with generous gutters and outside margins. No text, lines, ground, shadows, white matte, glow or particles. Genuine transparent alpha outside every silhouette. Dark matte pixel clusters and original materials.
